from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Section 1 Title and Lecture Lines
        title = "Prerequisite: The Geometry of a Single Transformation"
        lines = [
            "A matrix transformation moves vectors in 2D space.",
            "Meet Momo the Robot, standing on our grid.",
            "We apply this matrix to the entire space.",
            "Watch Momo stretch as the grid morphs.",
            "Notice where the basis vectors land."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        i_color = "#FF0000"
        j_color = "#00FF00"
        momo_color = "#88C0D0"
        matrix_color = "#FFFF00"
        grid_color = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # A matrix transformation moves vectors in 2D space.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(matrix_color)
        
        # Display Matrix A at the top
        # Replaced MathTex with Text to avoid FileNotFoundError: 'latex'
        matrix_a = Text("A = [[2, 0], [0, 0.5]]", color=matrix_color)
        self.place_in_area(matrix_a, 'A3', 'A4', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(Write(matrix_a))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Meet Momo the Robot, standing on our grid.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(matrix_color)
        
        # Coordinate system (White grid)
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-2.5, 2.5, 1],
            y_range=[-2.5, 2.5, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": grid_color, "stroke_width": 1, "stroke_opacity": 0.5}
        )
        self.place_in_area(plane, 'B1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Basis vectors
        i_hat = Arrow(plane.c2p(0,0), plane.c2p(1,0), buff=0, color=i_color, stroke_width=5)
        j_hat = Arrow(plane.c2p(0,0), plane.c2p(0,1), buff=0, color=j_color, stroke_width=5)
        
        # Replaced MathTex with Text to avoid FileNotFoundError: 'latex'
        i_label = Text("i", color=i_color, font_size=24, slant=ITALIC).next_to(i_hat.get_end(), RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        j_label = Text("j", color=j_color, font_size=24, slant=ITALIC).next_to(j_hat.get_end(), UP, buff=0.1)

        # Momo the Robot (stick figure)
        unit_len = np.linalg.norm(plane.c2p(1,0) - plane.c2p(0,0))
        
        head = Circle(radius=0.15 * unit_len, color=momo_color)
        body = Line([0, -0.15 * unit_len, 0], [0, -0.6 * unit_len, 0], color=momo_color)
        l_arm = Line([0, -0.3 * unit_len, 0], [-0.25 * unit_len, -0.25 * unit_len, 0], color=momo_color)
        r_arm = Line([0, -0.3 * unit_len, 0], [0.25 * unit_len, -0.25 * unit_len, 0], color=momo_color)
        l_leg = Line([0, -0.6 * unit_len, 0], [-0.15 * unit_len, -0.9 * unit_len, 0], color=momo_color)
        r_leg = Line([0, -0.6 * unit_len, 0], [0.15 * unit_len, -0.9 * unit_len, 0], color=momo_color)
        momo = VGroup(head, body, l_arm, r_arm, l_leg, r_leg)
        
        momo.move_to(plane.c2p(0, 0), aligned_edge=DOWN)

        self.play(Create(plane))
        self.play(Create(i_hat), Create(j_hat), Write(i_label), Write(j_label))
        self.play(Create(momo))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(matrix_color)
        self.play(Indicate(matrix_a))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(matrix_color)
        
        matrix_array = np.array([[2, 0], [0, 0.5]])
        
        i_final_pos = plane.c2p(2, 0)
        j_final_pos = plane.c2p(0, 0.5)

        self.play(
            plane.animate.apply_matrix(matrix_array),
            momo.animate.apply_matrix(matrix_array),
            i_hat.animate.apply_matrix(matrix_array),
            j_hat.animate.apply_matrix(matrix_array),
            i_label.animate.move_to(i_final_pos + [0.4, 0, 0]),
            j_label.animate.move_to(j_final_pos + [0, 0.4, 0]),
            run_time=3
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(matrix_color)
        
        self.play(
            Indicate(i_hat, color=i_color),
            Indicate(j_hat, color=j_color)
        )
        
        # Replaced MathTex with Text to avoid FileNotFoundError: 'latex'
        i_coord = Text("(2, 0)", color=i_color, font_size=18).next_to(i_label, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        j_coord = Text("(0, 0.5)", color=j_color, font_size=18).next_to(j_label, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Write(i_coord), Write(j_coord))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Sequential Challenge: Two Steps in a Row",
            [
                "- First, we rotate Momo 90 degrees counter-clockwise.",
                "- Next, we apply a horizontal shear to him.",
                "- Can we find one matrix for both steps?"
            ]
        )

        # Colors for consistency
        ROT_COLOR = "#58C4DD"  # Light blue
        SHEAR_COLOR = "#83C167"  # Light green
        MOMO_COLOR = "#FFD700"  # Gold/Yellow
        
        # Define Momo
        momo_body = Square(side_length=1, fill_opacity=0.5, color=MOMO_COLOR)
        eye_l = Dot(point=[-0.2, 0.2, 0], color=WHITE).scale(0.5)
        eye_r = Dot(point=[0.2, 0.2, 0], color=WHITE).scale(0.5)
        smile = Arc(radius=0.2, start_angle=-TAU/4 - 0.5, angle=1, color=WHITE)
        momo = VGroup(momo_body, eye_l, eye_r, smile)
        
        # Define the coordinate system (NumberPlane)
        # We want it to stay within the right side area (A1 to F6)
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            background_line_style={
                "stroke_color": GREY,
                "stroke_width": 2,
                "stroke_opacity": 0.5
            }
        )
        
        # Group Momo and Plane so they transform together
        transformation_group = VGroup(plane, momo)
        self.place_in_area(transformation_group, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Store original center for relative transformations
        group_center = transformation_group.get_center().copy()

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight first lecture line
        self.lecture[0].set_color(ROT_COLOR)
        self.add(transformation_group)
        
        # Rotation Matrix (90 deg CCW)
        rot_matrix = [[0, -1], [1, 0]]
        
        self.play(
            transformation_group.animate.apply_matrix(rot_matrix, about_point=group_center),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Revert first line color, highlight second
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(SHEAR_COLOR)
        
        # Horizontal Shear Matrix (k=1)
        shear_matrix = [[1, 1], [0, 1]]
        
        self.play(
            transformation_group.animate.apply_matrix(shear_matrix, about_point=group_center),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Revert second line color, highlight third
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Final emphasis - maybe a pulse or just showing the final result clearly
        self.play(
            transformation_group.animate.scale(1.1),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        self.play(
            transformation_group.animate.scale(1/1.1),
            run_time=0.5
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout("Function Composition Logic (The 'Right-to-Left' Rule)", [
            "- Transformations work like nested functions.",
            "- We apply A first, then B.",
            "- The first transformation matrix goes on the right."
        ])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display 'f(g(x))' and 'B(A(v))' with 'g' and 'A' in yellow (#FFFF00).
        # Replaced MathTex with VGroup of Text to avoid 'latex' dependency
        func_comp = VGroup(Text("f("), Text("g"), Text("(x))")).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.05)
        func_comp[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        mat_comp = VGroup(Text("B("), Text("A"), Text("(v))")).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.05)
        mat_comp[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        self.place_at_grid(func_comp, 'B2', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.place_at_grid(mat_comp, 'B5', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # Highlight first lecture line
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.play(Write(func_comp), Write(mat_comp))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show the equation Vector_final = B * A * Vector_initial in white (#FFFFFF).
        # Replaced MathTex with MarkupText/Text to avoid 'latex' dependency
        eq_v_final = MarkupText("v<sub>final</sub>")
        eq_equal = Text("=")
        eq_b = Text("B")
        eq_dot1 = Text("·")
        eq_a = Text("A")
        eq_dot2 = Text("·")
        eq_v_initial = MarkupText("v<sub>initial</sub>")
        
        equation = VGroup(eq_v_final, eq_equal, eq_b, eq_dot1, eq_a, eq_dot2, eq_v_initial).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.15)
        self.place_in_area(equation, 'D1', 'D6', scale_factor=1.1)
        
        # Transition highlight to second lecture line
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.play(Write(equation))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Animate a glow moving from Vector_initial to matrix A, then to matrix B.
        # Transition highlight to third lecture line
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # Creating a glow effect using a Highlight Rectangle
        glow = SurroundingRectangle(eq_v_initial, color="#FFFF00", buff=0.1)
        glow.set_stroke(width=4, opacity=0.8)
        
        self.play(Create(glow))
        self.play(glow.animate.move_to(eq_a), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(Indicate(eq_a, color="#FFFF00"))
        self.play(glow.animate.move_to(eq_b), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(Indicate(eq_b, color="#FFFF00"))
        self.play(FadeOut(glow))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Fetching titles and lines from storyboard
        title_text = "Visualizing the Composition via Basis Vectors"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Trace i-hat's path through the first transformation.",
            "Follow its journey through the second step.",
            "These final coordinates become our first column.",
            "Repeat this entire process for j-hat.",
            "The combined matrix is now complete."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_I = "#FF0000"  # Red for i-hat
        COLOR_J = "#00FF00"  # Green for j-hat
        
        # Create Coordinate System
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            x_length=3.5,
            y_length=3.5,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True},
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.4}
        )
        self.place_in_area(plane, "C3", "F6")
        self.add(plane)
        
        # Create Matrix C structure using Text to avoid FileNotFoundError: 'latex'
        matrix_label = Text("C = ", font_size=32)
        bracket_l = Text("[", font_size=40)
        bracket_r = Text("]", font_size=40)
        
        entry_11 = Text("?", font_size=32)
        entry_21 = Text("?", font_size=32)
        entry_12 = Text("?", font_size=32)
        entry_22 = Text("?", font_size=32)
        
        col1 = VGroup(entry_11, entry_21).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3)
        col2 = VGroup(entry_12, entry_22).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3)
        entries = VGroup(col1, col2).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5)
        
        matrix_group = VGroup(matrix_label, bracket_l, entries, bracket_r).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        self.place_in_area(matrix_group, "A3", "B5", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        # Basis vector labels above matrix
        label_i = Text("i", slant=ITALIC, color=COLOR_I, font_size=24).next_to(col1, UP, buff=0.2)
        label_j = Text("j", slant=ITALIC, color=COLOR_J, font_size=24).next_to(col2, UP, buff=0.2)
        
        self.add(matrix_group, label_i, label_j)
        
        # Define vectors
        def p(x, y): return plane.coords_to_point(x, y)
        
        vec_i = Vector([1, 0], color=COLOR_I)
        vec_i.put_start_and_end_on(p(0,0), p(1,0))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_I))
        self.play(Create(vec_i))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        self.play(
            vec_i.animate.put_start_and_end_on(p(0,0), p(0,1)),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_I))
        
        self.play(
            vec_i.animate.put_start_and_end_on(p(0,0), p(1,1)),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        res11 = Text("1", color=COLOR_I, font_size=32).move_to(entry_11)
        res21 = Text("1", color=COLOR_I, font_size=32).move_to(entry_21)
        
        self.play(
            Transform(entry_11, res11),
            Transform(entry_21, res21)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(COLOR_J))
        
        vec_j = Vector([0, 1], color=COLOR_J)
        vec_j.put_start_and_end_on(p(0,0), p(0,1))
        
        self.play(Create(vec_j))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        self.play(
            vec_j.animate.put_start_and_end_on(p(0,0), p(-1,0)),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        self.play(
            Indicate(vec_j, scale_factor=1.2, color=COLOR_J),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        res12 = Text("-1", color=COLOR_J, font_size=32).move_to(entry_12)
        res22 = Text("0", color=COLOR_J, font_size=32).move_to(entry_22)
        
        self.play(
            Transform(entry_12, res12),
            Transform(entry_22, res22)
        )
        
        # Box the matrix
        box = SurroundingRectangle(matrix_group, color=YELLOW, buff=0.2)
        self.play(Create(box))
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(Scene):
    """
    Expert implementation of Matrix Multiplication as Composition of Linear Transformations.
    This scene demonstrates how applying matrix A followed by matrix B is equivalent 
    to applying the product matrix BA.
    """
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Setup Layout (Title and Text content)
        title = Text("Matrix Multiplication as Composition", font_size=32, color=WHITE)
        title.to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        
        lecture_points = VGroup(
            Text("- Start with vector v", font_size=22),
            Text("- Apply Matrix A (Rotation)", font_size=22),
            Text("- Apply Matrix B (Scaling)", font_size=22),
            Text("- Result: T(v) = (B \u00b7 A) v", font_size=22)
        ).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT, buff=0.4)
        lecture_points.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.7)

        # 2. Setup Coordinate System (Right Side)
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            x_length=5,
            y_length=5,
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.4}
        ).to_edge(RIGHT, buff=1.0)
        
        origin = plane.coords_to_point(0, 0)
        
        # 3. Define the Vector
        # Initial vector v = [1, 1]
        v_coords = np.array([1, 1, 0])
        v_pointer = Vector(plane.coords_to_point(1, 1) - origin, color=YELLOW).shift(origin)
        v_label = Text("v", color=YELLOW, font_size=24).next_to(v_pointer.get_end(), UR, buff=0.1)

        # 4. Define Transformations (3x3 for Manim compatibility)
        # Matrix A: 90-degree counter-clockwise rotation
        matrix_a = [[0, -1, 0], 
                    [1,  0, 0], 
                    [0,  0, 1]]
        
        # Matrix B: Scaling x by 2
        matrix_b = [[2, 0, 0], 
                    [0, 1, 0], 
                    [0, 0, 1]]

        # 5. Animation Sequence
        self.play(Write(title))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Step 1: Initial Vector
        self.play(FadeIn(lecture_points[0]))
        self.play(Create(plane), Create(v_pointer), Write(v_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # Step 2: Apply Transformation A
        self.play(FadeIn(lecture_points[1]))
        self.play(
            v_pointer.animate.apply_matrix(matrix_a, about_point=origin),
            v_label.animate.move_to(plane.coords_to_point(-1.2, 1.2)),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # Step 3: Apply Transformation B
        self.play(FadeIn(lecture_points[2]))
        # Note: apply_matrix applies relative to current state
        self.play(
            v_pointer.animate.apply_matrix(matrix_b, about_point=origin),
            v_label.animate.move_to(plane.coords_to_point(-2.2, 1.2)),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # Step 4: Conclusion
        self.play(FadeIn(lecture_points[3]))
        
        # Highlight the final result
        rect = SurroundingRectangle(lecture_points[3], color=BLUE, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(rect))
        self.play(Indicate(v_pointer, color=BLUE))
        
        self.wait(3)

outline.topic: Matrix Multiplication as Composition of Linear Transformations
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate students or advanced high school students with basic algebra knowledge

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Geometry of a Single Transformation
sections.content: Briefly review that a 2D matrix multiplication (A * v) represents a linear transformation. Visually demonstrate how a grid transforms when basis vectors i-hat (1,0) and j-hat (0,1) move to new coordinates. Introduce 'Momo the Robot' standing on the grid to show how his shape stretches or rotates.
sections.example: Momo the Robot is scaled by factor 2 horizontally and 0.5 vertically. The matrix A = [[2, 0], [0, 0.5]] represents this single transformation.

sections.title: The Sequential Challenge: Two Steps in a Row
sections.content: Introduce the scenario where Momo needs to undergo two transformations sequentially. First, a 90-degree rotation (Transformation A), followed by a horizontal shear (Transformation B). Show the grid morphing twice in a sequence. Define the goal: Can we find a single 'Master Matrix' that does both at once?
sections.example: Momo first rotates 90 degrees left, then gets pushed (sheared) to the right. We track his position after step 1, then apply step 2 to that new position.

sections.title: Function Composition Logic (The 'Right-to-Left' Rule)
sections.content: Explain that matrix multiplication works like function nesting: f(g(x)). If we apply transformation A first, then B, the math looks like B(A(v)). This explains why, in the product BA, the matrix representing the first action is written on the right.
sections.example: Written as Vector_final = [Shear Matrix] * ([Rotation Matrix] * Vector_initial). The right-most matrix is the 'first responder'.

sections.title: Visualizing the Composition via Basis Vectors
sections.content: Demonstrate that the columns of the resulting matrix C (where C = BA) are simply the results of tracking where the original i-hat and j-hat end up after both transformations are applied. Use animation to follow the path of i-hat from (1,0) -> A(i-hat) -> B(A(i-hat)).
sections.example: If A rotates i-hat to (0,1) and B shears (0,1) to (1,1), then the first column of the combined matrix C is (1,1).

sections.title: Why Order Matters (Non-Commutativity)
sections.content: Use a visual example to show that changing the order of matrices changes the result. This is a critical property of matrix multiplication. Rotate then Shear is not the same as Shear then Rotate.
sections.example: Show Momo: (1) Rotating then (2) Shearing results in him leaning diagonally. (1) Shearing then (2) Rotating results in him leaning vertically. The visuals are distinct, proving AB ≠ BA.

sections.title: Summary: The Computational Shortcut
sections.content: Conclude that matrix multiplication is not just a bunch of dot products; it is the mathematical 'glue' that fuses multiple spatial actions into one. This allows computers to calculate complex 3D animations (like Momo jumping and spinning) using a single pre-calculated matrix.
sections.example: In video games, a character's rotation, scaling, and movement are all multiplied into one 'Model Matrix' to render the frame efficiently.
